title: SS27 Boys' Material Innovations
summary: Materials for boys: UPF swim and jersey, recycled performance knits, quick-dry and sand-free fabrics.
research_period: Pitti Bimbo 103, Florence, 24-25 June 2026; Playtime Paris, 28-30 June 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Premium and mid-market childrenswear, Europe-led fairs, global retail

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Swimwear, T-shirts and accessories with built-in UV filters were prominent and are becoming common, linked to family concern for health and to changing climate<sup>[1]</sup>
- Newer lines emphasise breathability, quick drying and comfort; childrenswear is moving toward functionality, material quality and durability<sup>[1]</sup>
- Teeter Totter showed UPF50+ swim and sportswear, backpacks and ultra-light, sand-free beach towels<sup>[2]</sup>
- Collections increasingly use recycled fibres, organic cotton and certified materials<sup>[1]</sup>

sections.heading: Readiness
sections.body:
| Material | Readiness |
|---|---|
| UPF jersey and swim | Ready; test and label |
| Recycled polyester track fabric | Ready |
| Quick-dry mesh | Ready |

design_implications:
- Test UPF to a recognised standard.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, snaps and decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
